body:
## Context / Why

While fixing hearsay-tools/cezarion#1139 with Squeal 0.1.199, a small policy unit test completed its red/green cycle. After tightening one assertion, repeated `status --wait 60000 packages/cezar/src/delegation/policy.test.ts` calls timed out because the selected file remained queued behind broader validation. The final focused verdict arrived several minutes later. The daemon was alive throughout.

The agent needed that one test's result to commit the fix. A named wait described its pending state accurately but did not help the requested file run sooner. This blocked a small change behind unrelated long-running files.

## What needs to be done

Give a named test wait an explicit way to prioritize its selected queued files, without rerunning current results or interrupting tests already running. Document whether named waits promote work automatically or require a separate option.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An agent can prioritize the queued files selected by a named wait before unrelated queued files.
- [ ] Already running work completes normally, and unrelated pending work remains queued.
- [ ] Current results are reused instead of forcing duplicate runs.
- [ ] CLI output explains whether selected files are running, prioritized in the queue, or waiting for a separate constraint.
- [ ] A regression covers a short selected test queued behind broader work.

## Related links

- https://github.com/hearsay-tools/cezarion/pull/1172
- https://github.com/hearsay-tools/squeal/issues/4 concerns ranking slow specs by inferred relevance; this report concerns an explicitly named fast test.
title: Prioritize explicitly awaited test files over queued background work
